newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares snap losing streak, stage rebound.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares snap losing streak, stage rebound.

text.p: Slovenian shares reversed an eight-day losing streak on Thursday, rebounding 2.41 percent on the perception prices may have bottomed out, traders said.
"It seems prices have bottomed out. A further rebound could be in store tomorrow as well but next week the market will likely consolidate unless there're fresh incentives," one said.
The SBI index rose 32.84 points to 1,394.91. During the last eight trading sessions the index had lost 7.2 percent.
Market turnover rose to 136.8 million tolars from 117.8 million. Overall 14 shares rose, three fell and nine were untraded.
Bank SKB had the highest turnover, firming 0.44 percent to 57,000 tolars on volume of 678 shares for total turnover of 38.9 million tolars.
"In the short-term SKB is likely to benefit the most due to discrepancy between its price in Ljubljana and the price of its GDRs in London," a broker said.
On Thursday, the GDRs, 20 of which represent one share, were trading around $36.25 -- nearly twice the price the shares trade at in Ljubljana.
Brokerage Primofin was the biggest gainer, jumping 8.57 percent to 13,300 tolars on volume of six shares.
Construction firm GPG led the day's decliners, falling 7.86 percent to 6,450 tolars on volume of 182 shares.
